newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates slightly off, eyes on overnight.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates slightly off, eyes on overnight.

text.p: Interbank rates were slightly lower on Thursday morning as lending by local and foreign banks continued to pressure rates, dealers said.
But market focus is on the overnight rate, they said.
"It will be interesting to see how the overnight trade later today. By then we will know whether there is a large outflow or not," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Dealers have said that there will be a Bank Negara lending maturity, said to be for two billion ringgit, on Thursday.
Such a maturity should push rates higher.
One-month money was at 7.35/40 percent against 7.40 percent on Wednesday, and three-month at 7.50 percent against 7.55.
One-week money was steady at 6.60/70 percent.
Dealers were expecting the overnight to trade between 5.8 and 7.0 percent.
The rate has been at 5.8 percent in the last three days due to aggressive lending by banks which were long on the overnight.
Interbank rates have also been pressured by improved liquidity following maturity of Bank Negara bills worth a total two billion ringgit over the past week which were not rolled over.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were higher across the board on the softening of interbank rates in the cash market.
At 0300 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up nine points to 92.65, or an implied yield of 7.35 percent.
The December contract rose seven to 92.74, or 7.26 percent and March 1998 was also up seven to 92.81, or 7.19 percent.
